Load libraries

library(amt)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(geosphere)
library(ggspatial)

Read the data

We are reading the raw dog movement data housed at Movebank to see if the outliers flagged by movebank are correct or not

raw_data <- read.csv(here("Telemetry data", "Free-ranging dogs - vksanj - Mudumalai TR - GPS collaring.csv"))
raw_data$timestamp <-as.POSIXct(raw_data$timestamp, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
                               tz = "Asia/Calcutta")
glimpse(raw_data)

Data processing

We want to do basic processing of the data (NA removal, HDOP and speed filtering) We are also converting the data into spatial format and plot them simultaneously to check for the speed and manually marked outliers.

  • 4146 points are dropped because of NA location i.e. when the collar could not communicate successfully with the satellite.
  • 4 points were dropped as they were imprecise (HDOP >10 m).
  • The remaining points were processed in the next step through visualization.
data_df <- raw_data |> 
  drop_na(location.long) |> 
  filter(gps.hdop <10) |>
  group_by(individual.local.identifier) |>
  arrange(timestamp) |>
  mutate(
  step_length = distHaversine(cbind(location.long, location.lat), 
                              cbind(lag(location.long), lag(location.lat))),  # in meters
  time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(timestamp, lag(timestamp), units = "secs")),
  speed_mps = step_length / time_diff)|>
  ungroup()
data_df$speed_mps[is.na(data_df$speed_mps)]<-0

ggplot(data_df)+
  geom_histogram(aes(x = speed_mps), fill = "skyblue", breaks = c(0, 1,2, 5,10,25,50))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5, linetype=3)+
  labs(x = "Speed (m/s)")+
  theme_bw()

data_sf <- data_df |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("location.long", "location.lat"), crs = 4326)

Data visualization

Here we are visualizing all the individual dog tracks to see if there are any outliers and how the points marked with outliers are marked correctly The green points are marked as outlier by the speed filter of 5 m/s.

data_track <- data_sf |>
  group_by(individual.local.identifier) |>
  summarise(do_union = FALSE) |>
  st_cast("LINESTRING")

ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data = data_track)+
  annotation_map_tile(type = "osm") + 
  geom_path(data = data_df, aes(x = location.long, y = location.lat, col = speed_mps, 
                                group= individual.local.identifier), linewidth=1)+
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma")+
  geom_sf(data = data_sf, aes(fill = algorithm.marked.outlier), shape=21)+
  annotation_scale(location = "br")+
  labs(fill = "Speed outlier", col = "Speed (m/s)")+
  theme_bw()
## Zoom: 10

We can clearly see some outliers from the animal track and the histogram plot of speed We drop the locations and plot again to see how the tracks look like. The plot histogram looks much better and represents a distribution pattern that ecologically looks much better compared to the previous histogram.

data_df <- data_df |> filter(speed_mps < 5) |>
  filter(location.long> 76.6 & location.lat > 11.52)
data_df$manually.marked.outlier[data_df$manually.marked.outlier==""]<- "false"
glimpse(data_df)

## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value with `binwidth`.

Convert the animal track again into sf format and check the plot for outliers. Now we want to see manually marked outliers to see how they are distributed.

data_sf <- data_df |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("location.long", "location.lat"), crs = 4326)

ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data = data_track)+
  annotation_map_tile(type = "osm") + 
  geom_path(data = data_df, aes(x = location.long, y = location.lat, col = speed_mps, 
                                group= individual.local.identifier), linewidth = 1)+
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma")+
  geom_sf(data = data_sf, aes(fill = manually.marked.outlier), shape=21)+
  annotation_scale(location = "bl")+
  coord_sf(ylim = c(11.54, 11.62), xlim =  c(76.62, 76.72))+
  labs(fill = "Manually marked\noutlier", col = "Speed (m/s)")
## Zoom: 12

In this step, we are plotting the sampling duration for each dogs to check how the temporal pattern look like In particular, we are looking for large gaps in the data that may bias our results.

ggplot(data_df) +
  geom_point(aes(x = timestamp, y = individual.local.identifier), size = 0.5) +
  labs(x= "Time", y= "Individual_id")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme_bw()

Temporal summary analysis

We are creating an individual-wise track data from the movement data

### create amt track data from the movement data 
track_dat <- data_df %>%
  arrange(individual.local.identifier, timestamp) %>%
  mk_track(location.long, location.lat, timestamp, 
           Name = individual.local.identifier,
           crs = 4326)  # CRS 4326 is the coordinate reference system

### I am looking for the fix interval rates across individual to see if there is 
### any large gap in the data 
mov_datsum <- track_dat %>% nest(data=-"Name") %>% 
  mutate(data = map(data, ~ summarize_sampling_rate(.x, time_unit = "min"))) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Name , data) %>% 
  unnest(cols = data) %>% print(n =Inf)

We can see individuals like Rambo, Tony, Blackie and Pied do not have a lot of data and the data are very scattered across the sampling duration, which we do not want to use in the analysis further as the inference may not be robust.
